Trossard leaves Arsenal as club considers left-wing options

Published 14 July 2026 · Updated 6 September 2026 Premier League TV96 Live Editorial Team Sourced news summary and analysis · 3 min read
Back to News & Guides

Archive summary: the reporting below reflects the dated sources listed at the end. Interpretive sections are TV96 Live analysis, not independent or exclusive reporting.

Leandro Trossard has completed a permanent move from Arsenal to Beşiktaş, ending a productive spell in north London and opening a new stage of his career in Türkiye.

Sky Sports reported the transfer at £17 million, comprising an initial £15.3 million with a further £1.7 million in potential add-ons. The move gives Beşiktaş an experienced attacking player while allowing Arsenal to reshape an area of their squad ahead of the new season.

What Trossard leaves behind

Trossard departs with 174 Arsenal appearances, 36 goals and 34 assists, figures attributed to the club's record of his time there. The balance between goals and assists shows that his contribution was not limited to one type of attacking action. He could finish moves himself and help create opportunities for teammates.

During Arsenal's most recent title-winning campaign, he registered eight goals and 11 assists in 50 appearances as the team also reached the Champions League final. That season offered a clear example of his usefulness across a demanding schedule: he supplied output while Arsenal competed deep into major competitions.

At 31, Trossard moves with extensive Premier League and European experience. Beşiktaş are therefore acquiring a player accustomed to high-level expectations rather than a prospect who still needs to establish a senior record. The important question is how quickly that experience translates into his new environment.

Why the transfer suits Beşiktaş

The appeal for Beşiktaş is straightforward. Trossard arrives with recent production and experience of matches carrying significant pressure. His recorded totals suggest he can contribute in more than one way, giving his new club options when constructing its attack.

Those numbers do not guarantee an identical return in a different league. Changes of team, tactical demands and adaptation can all affect output. A fair assessment will depend on his role, minutes and connection with new teammates rather than simply transferring his Arsenal averages to Beşiktaş.

Arsenal's next decision

For Arsenal, the departure creates room but also removes a proven source of goals and assists. Sky Sports reported that Morgan Rogers was a priority target and that Bradley Barcola and Christos Tzolis were among other players considered as the club examined left-sided attacking options. Interest in possible replacements should still be distinguished from a completed signing.

That distinction matters because squad planning can change during a transfer window. Arsenal may replace Trossard directly, distribute his minutes among existing players or adjust the profile they seek. Whatever route they choose, his 70 combined goals and assists for the club set a measurable level of production to address.

Beşiktaş, meanwhile, can judge the deal on more than headline numbers. How Trossard links with the team's other attackers, handles the rhythm of a new competition and contributes over a full campaign will determine whether the transfer delivers its intended sporting value.

The completed transfer closes one question and creates two new ones: how Beşiktaş will use an experienced attacker, and how Arsenal will respond to his departure. Those outcomes will become clearer only after the new season begins.
